verdict.rationale: Proton Pass documents built-in TOTP generation for saved logins and passkey prompting with a site pop-up. It ships Chromium and Firefox browser extensions and markets credential autofill. A community post also references Proton's claim of '2FA autofill'. However, no first-party doc explicitly shows the extension auto-inserting TOTP codes into login fields, and passkey use is described only as a prompt. Missing for 10: explicit first-party documentation of TOTP autofill in the browser extension, a clear statement that passkey sign-in happens inside the extension, and hands-on corroboration of either working during login.

support.subject: As an everyday user, a browser extension autofills my TOTP codes and passkeys during login instead of making me retype them

citations.quote: Proton Pass can securely generate TOTP codes for websites that you have saved login details for.
Next time you access the site, Proton Pass will prompt you to enter using your passkey.
they will all be displayed in the same pop-up, and you can choose which to use.
Securely store, share, and autofill your credentials with Proton Pass
The Chrome browser extension also works on Chromium-based browsers, including Edge, Brave, Chromium, Opera, and Vivaldi.
